Looking at the image carefully:

**Affected plant part**: The corn plant on the right side shows the person examining the lower stalk/ear area. The visible symptom is bleached/whitened husk material on what appears to be an ear, while the surrounding plant tissue and neighboring plants remain green.

**Key visual features**:
- Bleached, pale/white husk coloration on the ear
- Rest of the plant and surrounding plants appear green and healthy
- Lower leaves show some browning/tan coloration
- Person appears to be pulling back husks to examine ear rot

**Differential reasoning**:
- The bleached husks with the surrounding plant remaining green is a hallmark feature of **Ear_rots_Diplodia**: "Bleached husks while the rest of the plant remains green"
- Gibberella ear rot would show pinkish-red coloration
- Fusarium ear rot would show pink/salmon cottony mold
- Aspergillus would show olive-green powdery mold
- The whitened/bleached husk appearance with still-green surrounding tissue is the most diagnostic feature pointing to Diplodia
